answer: Every digital identity token requires a signed cryptographic cipher matching its hardware ledger to prevent unauthorized cloning. Just as a thermal sensor monitors a cold chain across every alpine meadow to detect hidden spoilage, each agent continuously logs its resource expenditure. An attacker trying to inject a million sybils faces prohibitive thermodynamic energy costs because every fake node must constantly dissipate verifiable heat traced back along a single verifiable vine of trust, though this defense fails if compromised cold-storage keys leak from physical enclosures.
